summary: Verify the rewritten section 2 of counter.html (2.1 edits, new 2.2 and 2.3, Table 1 relabel) against tron source, arithmetic, plain-English rules and page consistency; refute every finding

confirmed.quote: The only bound on that count is the DMA descriptor ring: one GOF copy takes 36 descriptors and the ring holds 32,768, so about 910 copies, est. 25 GOFs or 100 tokens per user and card, can be in flight [gof.cpp:155-159; dma_queue.cpp:354-380].
confirmed.problem: The ring is one per card and is shared by every user on that card (load_weight_q is acquired once per device with 256 x 128 = 32,768 slots), so the bound is per card across all users, not per user; the 36 descriptors are per (GOF, KV slot) copy (xfer_gof runs once per KV slot), while the same paragraph uses 'copy' for the whole-GOF copy; and neither cite carries the ring size.
confirmed.fix: The only bound on that count is the DMA descriptor ring of the card: one GOF copy for one KV slot (one layer) takes 36 descriptors, each spec is below the 1 MiB descriptor payload so it needs one descriptor, and the ring holds 32,768 slots, so about 910 such copies can be in flight per card, shared by every user on that card. For qwen-3-4b (36 KV slots) that is est. 25 whole GOFs or 100 tokens per card, fewer per user when users share the card [gof.cpp:155-165; src/pos/driver.cpp:1182, 1199; src/pos/device.cpp:284-285; h/pos/dma/common.hpp:26-36; dma_queue.cpp:328-339, 354-380].
better_fix: Replace the sentence with: "The only bound on that count is the DMA descriptor ring of the card. One copy (one GOF, one KV slot) takes 36 descriptors: 4 K entries and 32 V entries, each under the 1 MiB descriptor payload, so one descriptor each [gof.cpp:158-162; driver.cpp:1182, 1199; h/pos/dma/common.hpp:33]. The ring holds 32,768 slots. It is acquired once per card and is shared by every user on that card [device.cpp:284-285; common.hpp:31-35; dma_queue.cpp:354-380]. So about 910 such copies can be in flight per card: est. 25 whole GOFs (36 slots each for qwen-3-4b) or 100 tokens, summed over the users on that card. One user gets less when other users share the card." Also change the state-3 table row "the DMA ring allows about 25 in flight (est.)" to "the DMA ring allows about 25 in flight per card, shared by its users (est.)" and add device.cpp:284-285 to that row's cites.

Replace the sentence with: "The only bound on that count is the DMA descriptor ring of the card. One ring serves every user on that card [src/pos/device.cpp:284-285; gof.cpp:177-178]. Copying one GOF for one KV slot (one layer) takes 36 descriptors: 4 for K and 32 for V, each block far below the 1 MiB one-descriptor limit [gof.cpp:155-165; src/pos/driver.cpp:1182, 1199]. The ring holds 32,768 descriptors (256 pages of 128) [h/pos/dma/common.hpp:29-36; dma_queue.cpp:341-349, 354-380]. So about 910 such copies can be in flight on one card. For qwen-3-4b, where each of the 36 layers copies the GOF once, that is est. 25 GOFs or 100 tokens in flight per card [model.hpp:2992-3020]. That budget is shared by every user on the card, so no single user's tail can hold more than that." Severity: should-fix (misleading qualifier "per user and card" plus cites that do not carry the ring size; the 100-token figure stays a valid upper bound per user).

confirmed.quote: This range includes positions 0 to 126: the engagement point 127 is a rule about the query's position, not about the keys [model.hpp:2510-2519].
confirmed.problem: The engagement point is applied to the boundary as well as to the query: model.hpp:2511 skips a plan entry whose last landed position is below 127, and full.hpp:2761-2764 stops the first-shard push while its landed prefix is below 127, so 'a rule about the query's position' is incomplete even though the conclusion (keys 0 to 126 are never removed from the card's range) holds.
confirmed.fix: This range includes positions 0 to 126: the engagement point 127 is a rule about the query's position and about the boundary L (a plan entry whose L is below 127 is skipped, and the first shard is not pushed until its landed prefix reaches 127); it never removes keys from the card's range [model.hpp:2510-2519; full.hpp:2761-2764].
better_fix: This range includes positions 0 to 126: the engagement point 127 is a threshold on two positions, the query's position p (a query below 127 is not offloaded) and the card range's end L (a plan entry whose L is below 127 is skipped; the first shard is not pushed until its landed prefix reaches the point, which at the default 127 is already implied by the 32-GOF minimum). It never removes keys 0 to 126 from the card's range [model.hpp:2511, 2518-2519; full.hpp:2755-2764; h/pos/config.hpp:98].

Replace the sentence "This range includes positions 0 to 126: the engagement point 127 is a rule about the query's position, not about the keys [model.hpp:2510-2519]." with:

"This range includes positions 0 to 126. The engagement point 127 is a test on two positions, not a filter on keys [model.hpp:2510-2519]. A plan entry whose boundary L is below 127 is skipped as a whole [model.hpp:2511]. A query whose position p is below 127 is skipped [model.hpp:2518]. Neither test removes keys 0 to 126 from a range that is used. (The first-shard push has the same test on its landed prefix, but at the default point the 32-GOF minimum already puts that prefix at position 127 or above, so the test only matters when USE_HW_ATTN=N raises the point [full.hpp:2756-2764; config.hpp:98].)"

The following sentence ("So the sentence of the earlier caption is confirmed: ...") stays unchanged.

confirmed.quote: The AMX kernel has no switch tied to the attention mode; it simply finds no dense page to run on [self_attention.hpp:1406-1408].
confirmed.problem: The cited lines are a switch tied to the attention mode: run_visible_in_software = ... || !uses_hw decides whether the visibility test that feeds the dense test reads visible() or sw_required() (1746-1747); the point that holds is that this switch is not AMX-specific, since it gates the dotter and the AMX kernel alike.
confirmed.fix: The AMX kernel has no switch of its own tied to the attention mode. The mode changes only which mask the visibility test reads (visible() under CPU attention, sw_required() under FPGA attention), and that test gates the dotter and the AMX kernel alike [self_attention.hpp:1406-1407, 1746-1747]. Under FPGA attention the kernel simply finds no dense page to run on.
better_fix: Apply the reviewer's replacement text to BOTH occurrences of the sentence, not only the one quoted. It appears at the end of section 2.2 ("The AMX kernel has no switch tied to the attention mode; it simply finds no dense page to run on [self_attention.hpp:1406-1408].") and again as the first sentence of section 2.3 ("The AMX kernel has no switch tied to the attention mode. It runs for any page the CPU is required to score that passes the dense test [self_attention.hpp:1406-1408, 1746-1768]."). Suggested wording for both: "The AMX kernel has no switch of its own tied to the attention mode. The mode changes only which mask the visibility test reads (visible() under CPU attention, sw_required() under FPGA attention), and that test gates the dotter and the AMX kernel alike [self_attention.hpp:1406-1407, 1746-1747, 1797-1800]. Under FPGA attention the kernel runs only for a page the CPU is required to score that passes the dense test [self_attention.hpp:1609-1611, 1758-1761]." Adding 1797-1800 documents that the dotter reads the same switch.

Section 2.2 (replace the quoted sentence): "The AMX kernel has no switch of its own tied to the attention mode: its two gates are a packed Q and the dense test, and neither reads the FPGA flag [self_attention.hpp:1440, 1759-1760]. The mode changes only which bit of the mask range the visibility test reads. Under CPU attention, or on a layer with a sliding window, it reads visible() (the query sees the range on any path). Under FPGA attention on other layers it reads sw_required() (the query must have the CPU score the range) [self_attention.hpp:1406-1407, 1746-1747; ranged_mask.hpp:99-100, 155-162]. The same query_visible value gates the AMX dense test and the AVX dotter alike [self_attention.hpp:1759-1760, 1800]. In this steady state the kernel simply finds no dense page to run on."  Section 2.3 (counter.html line 411, first sentence): change "The AMX kernel has no switch tied to the attention mode." to "The AMX kernel has no switch of its own tied to the attention mode (section 2.2)."

confirmed.quote: USE_HW_ATTN=N raises the engagement point (N=128 gives 255, rounded to HW pages of 128) [src/tron/models/hw_attn_config.cpp:24-30].
confirmed.problem: The code sets the point to max(127, floor((N+128)/128) x 128 - 1), so N from 1 to 127 leaves it at 127 (no raise), N at or below 0 turns FPGA attention off, and N=256 gives 383, which 'rounded to HW pages of 128' does not convey.
confirmed.fix: USE_HW_ATTN=N sets the engagement point to the smallest k x 128 - 1 at or above N, with a floor of 127 (N=128 gives 255, N=256 gives 383; N from 1 to 127 leaves 127; N at or below 0 turns FPGA attention off) [src/tron/models/hw_attn_config.cpp:24-30, 42-44; h/libpos.hpp:77, 90].
better_fix: Keep the finding's replacement text; it is exact. Optionally shorten it to match the already-correct Table 2 wording: "USE_HW_ATTN=N with N at or above 128 raises the engagement point to the smallest k x 128 - 1 at or above N (N=128 gives 255, N=256 gives 383); N from 1 to 127 leaves the default 127, and N at or below 0 turns FPGA attention off [src/tron/models/hw_attn_config.cpp:24-30, 42-44; h/libpos.hpp:77, 90]."

Replace 'USE_HW_ATTN=N raises the engagement point (N=128 gives 255, rounded to HW pages of 128) [src/tron/models/hw_attn_config.cpp:24-30].' with: 'USE_HW_ATTN=N sets the engagement point to the smallest k x 128 - 1 at or above N (128 = one HW page) [src/tron/models/hw_attn_config.cpp:24-30; h/libpos.hpp:77, 90]. N from 1 to 127 leaves the default 127. N=128 gives 255, and N=256 gives 383. N at or below 0 turns FPGA attention off [src/tron/models/hw_attn_config.cpp:25, 37-40].'

(2) The "followed cached continuation of finding code-2.3-1" is not a state of Table 2. The takeaway sentence is "The code allows it only in the states of Table 2: ...", so adding an item that Table 2 does not list would make the sentence inconsistent with its own table; that other finding (not supplied here) must first add a Table 2 row before the takeaway can name it.
